prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for B002 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific case has not weakened under scrutiny. It is a continuous arc from gut-hormone physiology (the incretin effect, proglucagon processing, the truncated insulinotropic peptide, receptor biology) to therapies whose effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes have been confirmed in several independent outcome trials over roughly two decades. Originality, mechanistic clarity, durability and impact are all strong, and recognition is timely rather than speculative. Holst carries the human physiology and the characterisation of the active forms, Drucker the receptor and proglucagon-peptide biology and its translation, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active peptide. No member has presented a case that a different achievement is stronger on the merits. The first-round responses sharpened the argument rather than changing it: the real decision is the third name and the wording of the citation, not whether B002 leads. I would also state that I judge this on the evidence about contribution, not on the fact that all six of us ranked it first.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weakest point and I cannot resolve it from the record available to me. Priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide among Mojsov, the Habener group and Holst is contested, and Habener is outside the credited list, so any trio omits someone with a credible claim. Excluding Knudsen is a judgement under the three-person cap and not a neutral choice. Her half-life extension work turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into once-daily and once-weekly drugs, and a prize that leaves her out honours the discovery of the mechanism more than the medicine patients take. A critic could say we reward the idea and skip the step that delivered the benefit. If the primary record shows that Mojsov's contribution to the active form is not independently established, the case for her slot weakens materially and I would move to Knudsen, with a citation that says plainly that the framing has shifted toward translation. Finally, long-term safety and durability of weight loss are still being characterised, though I do not think this touches the core discovery.

responses.point: Sandberg opened with Knudsen in the third slot, moved to the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio under the cap, and asks that the record say this is a judgement under the cap and not a finding that Knudsen's contribution is minor. He also argues that a disputed priority should not by itself disqualify a candidate.
responses.response: I agree with the wording he asks for and would put it in the committee's record: Knudsen is omitted because three names is the limit and we chose the discovery side, not because her work was minor. I also accept his argument that a contested priority is a reason to examine the record, not to drop a name by default, and I have been persuaded that treating dispute as disqualifying would reward the least careful narratives. Where I stay short of full agreement is on how much that settles. His point that the dispute is about emphasis and not about whether the work was done is plausible but unverified, and I hold it only until the primary record is checked. If that record turns against Mojsov's share in the active form, I would support his original configuration with Knudsen in the third slot, provided the citation names the translation framing openly.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps the discovery trio, calls the choice between Mojsov and Knudsen the actual decision on B002, and argues that B001 is more exposed to attribution objections than B002 because every trio omits someone credible.
responses.response: I agree with his framing of the B002 decision and with his judgement that B001 carries the heavier attribution burden. He has persuaded me on the substance of the B001 trio. In my opening I proposed Boyden, Nagel and Deisseroth, and I now think that was the weaker choice: leaving out Hegemann, whose characterisation of channelrhodopsin was decisive, is hard to defend, and I would use Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel if B001 had to be advanced, while accepting that Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck are then left out at a cost. That does not make B001 the preferred prize, because the attribution problem is a real reason it stays an alternative. I also keep my earlier disagreement with his view that Knudsen's work is simply industrial; Linnarsson is right that it required scientific invention, and the committee has to defend her exclusion on merit.

responses.point: Linnarsson says Knudsen's half-life extension required real scientific invention, so excluding her is defensible but not costless, and that Sandberg's configuration would become his fallback if the Mojsov evidence proved weak. He also reads B051 as promising but premature because no approved drug has followed.
responses.response: I accept his correction on Knudsen and have adjusted my own wording: I no longer describe her work as only development, and the final record should say that her omission has a cost. We differ a little on what follows. He treats a weak Mojsov finding as moving the third slot to Knudsen, and I agree, but I would not move the other two names, and I would want the discovery-to-translation shift stated in the citation. On B051 I agree with his maturity reading. The cGAS-STING pathway is conceptually clean and the Chen and Barber contributions are clear, but I ranked it fifth for the same reason: the disease-level and therapeutic evidence has not matured, and I do not think it displaces any candidate in a configuration this round.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius places B035 third and flags that Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is missing from the credited names, and she also raised the weight of therapeutic development versus principle in her ranking of B017.
responses.response: I accept her concern about B035 as decisive for fallback purposes. Her point goes further than the credit for Eshhar. A trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg combines two designers of the chimeric receptor therapy with a related but separate earlier achievement, adoptive cell transfer, and I cannot write a single citation that is accurate for all three without either overstating Rosenberg's role or writing out the origin of the concept. So if B002 stalls on credit, I would choose B001 as the fallback over B035, because its attribution problem is a choice among well-documented contributors, whereas B035 has a structural gap in the credited names. I do not claim B001 is clean. Her view that a Medicine prize should weigh demonstrated patient benefit is one I share, and it is why a tool prize remains a fallback and not my preference.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps B002 as a prize centred on the discovery of the mechanism, assigns Holst, Drucker and Mojsov distinct parts of the discovery core, and lists B035 ahead of B001 as the alternative.
responses.response: I agree with his description of the three distinct contributions and with his view that a mechanism-centred prize best matches what the prize has honoured. I diverge only on the order of the alternatives. He lists B035 first. After the discussion of the credit gap I rank B001 ahead of B035 as the better fallback, since the problem with B035 is that no three credited names fit a single accurate citation, and I have not heard a way to fix that within the cap. I would be willing to revisit this if someone presents a citation wording and trio for B035 that handles Eshhar and Rosenberg explicitly. His point that the clinical impact is still growing is the best argument for timeliness, and I share it.

uncertainties: Whether the primary record supports naming Mojsov for the identification and characterisation of the active truncated GLP-1 peptide, and how Habener's claim should be treated. I have not been able to verify this and have no basis to claim confidence.
If Mojsov is not supported, whether Knudsen alone should take the third slot, and whether the citation can say clearly that the framing has moved from discovery to translation.
Whether the citation wording credits the physiology and the active form without implicitly writing out Habener and Knudsen.

Whether, under the three-person cap, a single-part B002 prize is the right form, or whether any second distinct part would be better. I am not proposing one because no alternative has a cleaner attribution.
Long-term safety and durability of benefit for incretin therapies are still being characterised.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. No credited name on B002, B001 or B035 is documented as a collaborator or colleague of mine. My profile records roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1), and he is not a candidate, so no recusal issue arises. My postdoc with Paul Greengard is unrelated to any shortlisted candidate. My neuroscience and neuropharmacology background touches B001 by topic only, which I have tried to discount, and I note that in this round I moved away from my own opening B001 trio. I do not request recusal for any member.
